hypothesis: a low-complexity fixed allocation program can generalize across bodies and budgets without online router learning
control: exact per-layer Top-B random masks with identical realized sequence budgets and common training batches
execution: on-policy pre-FFN features; exact per-layer Top-B; padding excluded; gather/scatter; real AdamW; no router learning and no dense planning pass
primary_endpoint: program minus random sparse held-out loss at step 50 in every body-budget regime
secondary_endpoints: paired sparse accuracy at steps 25 and 50
executed matmul/attention FLOPs and separately estimated feature/selection operations

selection_rule.advance: at most one program, requiring a negative step-50 loss difference against random in all four regimes; if several qualify, select the smallest mean paired loss difference
selection_rule.kill: if no program wins in all four regimes, stop the fixed-program route and do not add evolution or tune programs on these results
selection_rule.after_selection: the selected unchanged program must complete longer development runs before any fresh-body confirmation or dense-fewer frontier experiment

prohibited: calling this 50-step screen Level 1, Level 2, or Level 3
selecting different programs for different bodies or budgets
using confirmation bodies for program discovery
claiming total-cost efficiency from this screen
silently treating estimated auxiliary operations as exact hardware FLOPs
